source.title: Dual Proteomics Strategies to Dissect and Quantify the Components of Nine Medically Important African Snake Venoms
locators: Section 5, Ethical statement, animal care and venoms' sampling
source.figure: Figure 4D, the outer values in the chart; inspected visually.

sample.composition: Pooled venom from multiple wild-caught specimens held in captivity.

measurement.method: Relative area of unique-peptide chromatographic peaks after trypsin-only digestion, grouped by parent toxin family; label-free shotgun LC-MS.
measurement.note: These are method-dependent abundance estimates, not direct measurements of protein mass. The paper also used MELD for identification; its identified-sequence proportions are a different measure and must not be mixed with these values.

completeness: The six outer-chart categories in Figure 4D sum to 100.00%; this is a complete transcription of the displayed figure groups, not a full molecular breakdown. Categories not separately displayed remain unknown and are not zero. The figure does not establish individual specimen pairing or cross-study measurement equivalence.
comparison_policy: This later Tanzanian pooled sample is not proven to be the same material as the 2015 Kenyan sample underlying the candidate earlier profile; do not overwrite, merge, or infer a correction to that measurement. Prefer this later primary study for evidence about this measured sample, not as a universal species composition.

reported_aggregate_categories.meaning: Non-toxins (including cellular components) and unknown proteins, as defined by the paper; not equivalent to an unidentified-toxins category.

limitations: The graphical summary contains an aggregate Others group, so not every protein or category is resolved.
Full quantitative supporting data were not accessed: publisher supplementary endpoint returned HTTP 429.
Species-specificity and mapping of source categories to existing controls require review.
